categories.name: Ethics
beliefs: Moral duties are absolute and cannot be overridden by consequences.
The morality of an action is determined solely by its outcomes.
Character and virtue matter more than rules or outcomes.
Every person deserves to be treated as an end in themselves.
What is ethical is whatever produces the greatest happiness for the most people.
Moral facts are objective and exist independently of what anyone believes.
Right and wrong are culturally constructed, not universal.
We have stronger moral duties to those close to us than to strangers.

categories.name: Epistemology
beliefs: Knowledge must ultimately be grounded in direct sensory experience.
Reason alone can yield genuine knowledge without relying on the senses.
We should proportion our belief to the available evidence.
All knowledge claims are provisional and subject to revision.
Intuition is a valid and irreplaceable source of knowledge.
Scientific consensus is the most reliable guide to empirical truth.
Expertise confers genuine epistemic authority and should be deferred to.
Personal experience is a more trustworthy guide than abstract theory.

categories.name: Politics
beliefs: Individual liberty should be constrained only to prevent harm to others.
Equality of outcome is as important as equality of opportunity.
A strong central government is necessary for a just and stable society.
Power should be decentralised and local communities should govern themselves.
Democracy is the only legitimate form of political authority.
Rights are natural and pre-political — governments cannot grant or take them.
Private property rights are foundational to a free society.
The state has a duty to redistribute wealth to reduce inequality.
National identity and shared culture are essential for social cohesion.

categories.name: Economics
beliefs: Free markets are the most efficient way to allocate resources.
Unregulated markets systematically produce harmful externalities.
Competition between firms drives innovation and benefits consumers.
Economic inequality is a natural and acceptable outcome of free exchange.
A universal basic income would improve human well-being and freedom.
Growth in GDP is a poor proxy for societal progress and well-being.
Globalisation raises living standards for everyone in the long run.
Governments should invest heavily in public goods and infrastructure.

categories.name: Metaphysics & Free Will
beliefs: Every event, including human choices, is determined by prior causes.
Humans possess genuine free will that transcends physical causation.
Free will and determinism are compatible — we can be free in a determined world.
Consciousness is entirely reducible to physical brain processes.
There is something it is like to be conscious that cannot be fully explained physically.
Personal identity persists through time as a continuous self.
The self is a useful fiction — there is no unchanging core identity.
Objective moral facts require a non-physical grounding to exist.

categories.name: Science & Technology
beliefs: Scientific progress is generally beneficial and should be accelerated.
Technology creates risks that outpace society's ability to govern them.
The precautionary principle should guide decisions under deep uncertainty.
Artificial intelligence poses an existential risk to humanity.
Nuclear energy is essential for a safe and low-carbon future.
Genetic engineering of humans crosses an ethical line that should not be crossed.
Open and transparent information flow is essential for a free society.
Some knowledge is dangerous enough that its pursuit should be restricted.

categories.name: Society & Culture
beliefs: Traditional institutions embody accumulated wisdom that should be preserved.
Progress requires questioning and sometimes dismantling inherited norms.
The family is the foundational unit of a healthy society.
Individuals should be free to define their own conception of a good life.
Diversity of viewpoints within institutions improves their decision-making.
Social trust is more valuable than formal legal enforcement.
Immigration enriches culture and strengthens economies.
Nations have the right to control their borders and set immigration policy.
